userStories.title: Fix child process environment inheritance
userStories.description: worker.ts lines 184 and 368 build env as { ...envOverrides, RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE: 'engine' } WITHOUT spreading process.env. When spawn() receives explicit env, it replaces the entire environment — child has no PATH, HOME, DATABASE_URL. This is the root cause of 'env: node: No such file or directory' when running worker standalone. Fix: spread process.env before envOverrides. Also strip 4 Claude env vars (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING) to match pipeline.ts behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: handlePipelineRun (line ~184) env construction spreads process.env before envOverrides: { ...process.env, ...envOverrides, RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE: 'engine' }
handlePipelineRetry (line ~368) applies the same fix
Both locations strip CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING from inherited env
Worker started standalone (cd backend && npm run worker) successfully spawns execution-engine child processes with working PATH
Child processes can access DATABASE_URL, HOME, and other expected env vars

userStories.title: Create all queues in both server and worker, including pipeline:cron
userStories.description: pg-boss v10 requires explicit createQueue() before send() or work(). Currently: (1) pipeline:cron queue never created — scheduler fails with 'Queue pipeline:cron not found', (2) Express server never calls createQueue() — if server starts before worker, boss.send('pipeline:run') returns null silently. Fix: extract shared ensureQueues(boss) function into pg-boss.ts that creates all 4 base queues. Call from both initBoss() (server) and start() (worker). createQueue() is idempotent. Also add createQueue before boss.schedule() calls in scheduler.ts for per-schedule cron queues.
acceptanceCriteria: New ensureQueues(boss) function in backend/src/lib/pg-boss.ts creates pipeline:run, pipeline:retry, pipeline:cancel, pipeline:cron queues
initBoss() in server calls ensureQueues() after boss.start() so server can send() before worker starts
worker.ts start() calls ensureQueues() before boss.work() registrations
scheduler.ts creates pipeline:cron queue before boss.schedule() at line ~161, and per-schedule queues before boss.schedule(name) at line ~186
Server started alone (without worker) can successfully send('pipeline:run', ...) without silent null return
Worker startup log no longer shows 'Queue pipeline:cron not found' error

userStories.title: Set proper expireInSeconds and disable pg-boss retries for pipeline jobs
userStories.description: Two bugs: (1) expire_in defaults to 900s (15 min) but pipeline runs take 30-60 min — jobs expire MID-RUN, get moved to failed, potentially retried spawning DUPLICATE execution engines. (2) retryLimit: 3 on boss.send() causes pg-boss to re-enqueue entire jobs, spawning NEW execution-engine processes. Wrong — execution-engine has its own per-story retry with model escalation. Fix: set expireInSeconds: 7200 (2 hours) for pipeline:run and pipeline:retry. Set retryLimit: 0. Set expireInSeconds: 120 for pipeline:cancel.
acceptanceCriteria: All boss.send('pipeline:run', ...) calls include expireInSeconds: 7200 and retryLimit: 0
All boss.send('pipeline:retry', ...) calls include expireInSeconds: 7200 and retryLimit: 0
All boss.send('pipeline:cancel', ...) calls include expireInSeconds: 120
No pipeline:run or pipeline:retry job has retryLimit > 0 anywhere in codebase
A pipeline run lasting 45 minutes does not expire or get retried by pg-boss
Cancel jobs that are not processed within 2 minutes expire harmlessly

userStories.title: Stale job recovery on worker startup
userStories.description: After worker crash, pgboss.job rows with state='active' are stuck. The 15-min default expiry (fixed to 2hr by WR-003) means the new worker can't pick up new jobs because old ones block the teamSize slots. Add recoverStaleJobs() called between initBoss() and boss.work(). Query pgboss.job for pipeline:run and pipeline:retry in state='active' whose started_on predates current worker startup. For each: fail the pgboss job via SQL, update pipeline_runs to 'failed', emit WAL event with reason 'worker_crash_recovery'. Do NOT re-queue — partially-executed runs may have committed code.
acceptanceCriteria: New recoverStaleJobs() function in worker.ts runs after initBoss()/ensureQueues() but before boss.work()
Queries pgboss.job for pipeline:run and pipeline:retry with state='active' AND started_on < worker startup timestamp
For each stale job: updates pgboss.job state to 'failed' and completed_on to NOW()
For each stale job: updates corresponding pipeline_runs row to status='failed' and finished_at=NOW()
For each stale job: emits WAL event 'run_finished' with reason: 'worker_crash_recovery'
Jobs started by the CURRENT worker instance (if any exist from a non-crash restart) are NOT touched
Each recovered job logged at WARN level with pgboss job ID and pipeline_runs ID
After recovery, new jobs are immediately picked up (teamSize slots freed)

userStories.title: Bidirectional pipeline_runs / pgboss.job state reconciliation
userStories.description: Manual SQL fixes to one table leave the other out of sync. Add reconcileState() that runs on startup (after WR-004's stale recovery) and every 60s. Case A: pipeline_runs.status IN ('running', 'queued') but NO matching pgboss job in state ('created', 'active', 'retry') — mark pipeline_runs as 'failed' and emit WAL. Case B: pgboss job state='active' for pipeline:run/pipeline:retry but pipeline_runs.status is NOT 'running' — fail the pgboss job. Log each mismatch at WARN.
acceptanceCriteria: New reconcileState() function in worker.ts runs after recoverStaleJobs() on startup
reconcileState() runs every 60s via setInterval during normal operation
Case A: pipeline_runs with status 'running' or 'queued' that have no corresponding pgboss.job in ('created', 'active', 'retry') are marked 'failed' with reason 'state_reconciliation'
Case B: pgboss.job with state 'active' for pipeline:run/pipeline:retry that have no corresponding pipeline_runs with status 'running' are failed via SQL
Each reconciliation action logged at WARN level with both pipeline_runs.id and pgboss.job.id
WAL events emitted for Case A failures so UI updates
Reconciliation interval cleaned up on shutdown (clearInterval)

userStories.title: Make cleanupOrphanRuns() bulletproof — server must never kill worker-managed runs
userStories.description: Rewrite cleanupOrphanRuns() in pipeline.ts (~line 4425). Current problems: (1) pgboss state check misses 'retry' state, (2) races with worker startup. New logic: (1) If any worker_heartbeat.last_seen within 90s, skip ALL cleanup — log 'Active worker detected, skipping orphan cleanup' and return 0. (2) If no active worker, check pgboss.job state IN ('created', 'active', 'retry') for each running pipeline_run — skip runs with matching pgboss jobs. (3) For runs with NO pgboss job AND no live PID (process.kill(pid, 0) throws), mark as 'failed'.
acceptanceCriteria: cleanupOrphanRuns() checks worker_heartbeat first — if any worker has last_seen within 90s, returns 0 with log message
When no active worker detected, pgboss.job query includes state 'retry' (was missing: only checked 'created', 'active')
PID liveness check via process.kill(pid, 0) before marking run as failed — only dead PIDs get cleaned
Server startup with active worker heartbeat does NOT touch any pipeline_runs
Server startup without worker and without pgboss jobs correctly cleans orphan runs
WAL event 'orphan_cleanup' emitted only for actually-cleaned runs (not skipped ones)
No race condition between server startup and worker startup (heartbeat check provides 90s safety window)

userStories.title: Graceful shutdown — kill child processes and clean up heartbeat
userStories.description: Rewrite shutdown() in worker.ts. Current: calls boss.stop() but leaves child processes running as orphans and leaves stale heartbeat. New flow: (1) set stopping=true, (2) SIGTERM all active child processes in activeProcesses map, (3) wait up to 15s for child processes to exit (poll activeProcesses.size === 0), (4) SIGKILL any remaining children, (5) update pipeline_runs.status to 'failed' for any runs still active, (6) DELETE this worker's heartbeat row, (7) boss.stop(timeout: 15000). Add process.on('uncaughtException') and process.on('unhandledRejection') handlers that call shutdown.
acceptanceCriteria: shutdown() sends SIGTERM to every process in activeProcesses map
Waits up to 15s for child processes to exit (polling at 500ms intervals)
After 15s, sends SIGKILL to any remaining child processes
pipeline_runs for any in-flight jobs updated to status='failed' with finished_at=NOW()
Worker heartbeat row deleted: DELETE FROM worker_heartbeat WHERE worker_id = $1
boss.stop({ timeout: 15_000 }) called after children are drained
process.on('uncaughtException') and process.on('unhandledRejection') both trigger shutdown()
Health endpoint no longer shows stale heartbeat data after clean worker shutdown

userStories.title: Worker auto-restart supervisor with exponential backoff
userStories.description: New file backend/src/worker-supervisor.ts. Lightweight supervisor that spawns worker.ts as child process and restarts on crash with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s). Reset backoff after 60s of stable operation. Exit code 0 = clean shutdown, no restart. Forward SIGTERM/SIGINT to child. Update package.json 'worker' script to run supervisor instead of worker directly.
acceptanceCriteria: New backend/src/worker-supervisor.ts spawns worker.ts as child process with stdio: 'inherit'
On non-zero exit code: restarts with exponential backoff starting at 1s, doubling each crash, max 30s
Backoff resets to 1s after 60s of continuous stable operation
On exit code 0: supervisor exits cleanly, no restart
SIGTERM and SIGINT forwarded to child worker process
backend/package.json 'worker' script updated to: 'npx tsx src/worker-supervisor.ts'
Root package.json dev:worker reference still works correctly with supervisor
Log output: '[supervisor] Worker exited with code N, restarting in Nms'

userStories.title: Fix pause endpoint ESRCH error and cancel endpoint dead-PID fallback
userStories.description: Two bugs found in production: (1) POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/pause returns HTTP 500 with 'Failed to send SIGTSTP: kill ESRCH' when the process group no longer exists (PID dead but run still marked 'running'). The isPidAlive(run.pid) check only tests the process itself, not the process group (-pid). Fix: wrap the process.kill(-run.pid, 'SIGTSTP') in a try/catch — if ESRCH, the process is already gone, return 409 with message 'Process is no longer running' rather than 500. (2) POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/cancel for 'running' runs sends a pipeline:cancel job to the worker, but if the worker is dead or the execution-engine PID is already gone, the DB never gets updated. Fix: in the cancel route, after sending the pg-boss job, also attempt process.kill(run.pid, 'SIGTERM') directly as a fallback — catch ESRCH and EPERM silently. If isPidAlive returns false immediately, mark the run as 'cancelled' in the DB directly without waiting for the worker.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/pause — when process.kill(-run.pid, 'SIGTSTP') throws ESRCH, returns HTTP 409 with { error: 'Process is no longer running' } instead of HTTP 500
POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/pause — when process.kill(-run.pid, 'SIGTSTP') throws EPERM (insufficient permissions), returns HTTP 500 with the original error message (existing behavior preserved)

POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/cancel (running path) — after sending pipeline:cancel to pg-boss, immediately checks if run.pid is alive; if not alive, marks pipeline_runs as 'cancelled' and finished_at=NOW() directly without waiting for worker
POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/cancel (running path) — if pid is alive, sends SIGTERM directly as a best-effort fallback alongside the pg-boss job; catches ESRCH/EPERM silently
Cancel of a run whose process is dead returns { ok: true, status: 'cancelled' } (not 'cancelling') and the run is immediately cancelled in DB
Existing cancel behavior for queued runs (remove pg-boss job, mark cancelled) is unchanged
No new 500 errors from either endpoint when PIDs are stale
